item.title: 2027: Engaging APC data boys, insult to my integrity — Pat Utomi
item.description: A chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Professor Pat Utomi, has described engaging social media users he accused of being All Progressives Congress (APC) supporters paid to troll critics as an insult to his integrity. Utomi said the users began attacking him after he raised concerns about the living and working conditions of Nigerian soldiers, whom he said were poorly paid despite risking their lives to protect the country. In a post on X on Sunday, the economist alleged that some of those who criticised him were APC supporters benefiting from what he described as “stomach infrastructure”. “Yesterday, we talked about the poor living and working conditions of Nigerian soldiers compared to their counterparts in the US, and how senators are fattening their pockets with billions of naira while the soldiers who risk their lives every day to protect us are underpaid heavily,” he wrote. He said some social media users attacked him after he raised the issue, prompting him to examine their profiles. “Then, some fellows benefiting from stomach infrastructure began to bash us. I took a quick look at their profiles, and it became obvious to me that they were APC data boys trolling anyone who dared to speak up,” Utomi said. He added that he would not engage with the accounts, saying, “Engaging with any of them is an insult to my integrity.” In a separate post, Utomi also accused APC politicians of attempting to intimidate Nigerians ahead of the 2027 general election. He said Nigerians should not allow such actions to discourage them from participating in the electoral process. “We have seen videos of APC politicians trying to intimidate Nigerians ahead of the 2027 general elections,” he wrote. Utomi urged Nigerians to unite and resist what he described as attempts to instil fear ahead of the polls. “Nigerians need to understand that these fellows are powerless when we stand united. Do not allow them to sow seeds of fear in you,” he said. He also called on voters to participate in the election and protect the integrity of their votes. “Come out, vote, and defend your votes,” Utomi added. item.title: 1,314 protesters arrested in France over unrest
item.description: Police arrested 1,314 people in weekend protests across France, the interior ministry said Sunday, adding that 53 officers were hurt in clashes. The arrests occurred as violence broke out on the margins of mass demonstrations in major cities on Saturday over the high cost of living. It was the second consecutive weekend of unrest in France, which is heading to presidential elections in April and May to choose a successor to Emmanuel Macron, who is reaching his two-term limit. The interior ministry said police responded to 75 fires during Saturday’s protests, adding that 24 shops were looted. “Several investigations have been opened,” it said in a statement, without giving details. It said that the rest of Saturday night, after the clashes had died down, was “calm”. The ministry statement on Sunday did not say how many protesters were hurt. Late Saturday, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez spoke of two serious injuries among protesters: one in Toulouse and one in Clermont-Ferrand. – Protesters hurt – The Toulouse prefecture, which reports to the interior ministry, told AFP that a 20-year-old man was seriously hurt with a wound to his hand. A street medic who tended demonstrators told AFP, on condition of anonymity, that the man had “several fingers” blown off his right hand. The prefecture covering Clermont-Ferrand said a man there also had a hand hurt, but did not suffer the loss of any fingers. A French regional daily, La Nouvelle Republique, reported that a man in Poitiers was hurt in his left eye, showing a photo of a man holding his face. The newspaper’s photographer told AFP he was a 19-year-old who was wounded during a charge by riot police firing stun grenades and tear gas. There have been several instances in recent weeks, during student protests in France, of people being maimed by police stun grenades or tear gas grenades. It was not known if the injuries reported from Saturday were from those police weapons. Officials said investigations had been opened in at least some of the cases. mk/rmb/sbk The post 1,314 protesters arrested in France over unrest appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Mother, child die as two container trucks overturn in Lagos
item.description: By Efe Onodjae A mother and her child have died after two heavily laden 20-foot container trucks overturned at Mile 2, near Freeman Market, inward Apapa, Lagos. The victims were trapped beneath the overturned trucks and their containers during the incident, which occurred over the weekend. The Lagos State Traffic Management Authority, LASTMA, said its rescue and recovery personnel responded to the scene to evacuate the victims and remove the wreckage. According to the agency, the road was temporarily cordoned off, while traffic was diverted through an adjoining service lane to ease congestion and prevent further accidents. LASTMA deployed a crane and a high-capacity tow vehicle to remove the overturned trucks and their cargoes, while officers of the Nigeria Police Force provided security during the operation. The remains of the victims were subsequently conveyed to the police mortuary in Yaba for necessary procedures. The General Manager of LASTMA, Mr Olalekan Bakare-Oki, expressed sadness over the incident and called for a thorough investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the accident. He urged relevant security agencies to determine whether mechanical defects, excessive loading, improper cargo distribution, driver negligence or other factors contributed to the incident. Bakare-Oki also called on truck operators to ensure their vehicles were roadworthy, secure their cargoes properly and comply with established road safety regulations. item.title: Troops neutralise 6 terrorists, arrest 11 suspected collaborators in Borno
item.description: Troops of the Nigerian Army have neutralised six terrorists, arrested 11 suspected collaborators and received the surrender of a Jama’atu Ahlis Sunna Lidda’awati wal-Jihad (JAS) member in Borno. This is contained in an operational report made available to the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN), on Sunday in Abuja. The report said the operations, conducted by troops of the Joint Task Force North-East, Operation Hadin Kai (OPHK), targeted terrorist fighters and suspected support networks in Kaga and Gwoza Local Government Areas. It said troops of 29 Task Force Brigade Garrison, supported by Hybrid Force personnel, ambushed suspected Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP)/JAS terrorists along the Targejeri axis of Kaga at about 12:37 a.m. on Oct. 25. According to the report, six terrorists were neutralised during the encounter, while troops recovered an AK-47 rifle, three magazines and 169 rounds of 7.62mm special ammunition. “Other recovered items included two Android phones, three button phones and charms. “In a related development, troops arrested six additional suspected terrorist collaborators during a follow-up raid in Benisheikh, Kaga, at about 6:20 a.m. on Oct. 24. “The arrests brought the number of suspects apprehended in connection with the investigation to 11, including five earlier arrests. “Items listed as recovered during the raid included an AK-47 rifle, three empty magazines, 169 rounds of 7.62mm special ammunition, three terrorist uniforms, a turban, a head mask, two Android phones, three button phones and charms,” it said. The report said the suspects were undergoing investigation to establish their alleged involvement in terrorist activities and identify possible links to other members of the network. It added that troops of 192 Battalion (Main), supported by Hybrid Force personnel at Hambagda Internally Displaced Persons (IDP) Camp in Gwoza, received a JAS member who surrendered at about 9:20 p.m. on Saturday. According to the report, preliminary investigation indicated that the individual had escaped from a terrorist enclave in the Mandara Mountains area of Gwoza and decided to abandon terrorism. “The individual surrendered with an AK-47 rifle and a magazine containing 28 rounds of 7.62mm special ammunition,” it added. The report said the defector was in custody undergoing further investigation and processing in line with established procedures. It said the operations underscore OPHK’s continued efforts to disrupt terrorist activities, dismantle support networks and encourage defections through sustained, intelligence-led operations. The military urged members of the public to provide credible and timely information to security agencies to support efforts to restore peace and enable displaced communities to return safely. The report said the operations, conducted by troops of the Joint Task Force North-East, Operation Hadin Kai (OPHK), targeted terrorist fighters and suspected support networks in Kaga and Gwoza Local Government Areas. It said troops of 29 Task Force Brigade Garrison, supported by Hybrid Force personnel, ambushed suspected Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP)/JAS terrorists along the Targejeri axis of Kaga at about 12:37 a.m. on Oct. 25. According to the report, six terrorists were neutralised during the encounter, while troops recovered an AK-47 rifle, three magazines and 169 rounds of 7.62mm special ammunition. “Other recovered items included two Android phones, three button phones and charms. “In a related development, troops arrested six additional suspected terrorist collaborators during a follow-up raid in Benisheikh, Kaga, at about 6:20 a.m. on Oct. 24. “The arrests brought the number of suspects apprehended in connection with the investigation to 11, including five earlier arrests. “Items listed as recovered during the raid included an AK-47 rifle, three empty magazines, 169 rounds of 7.62mm special ammunition, three terrorist uniforms, a turban, a head mask, two Android phones, three button phones and charms,” it said. The report said the suspects were undergoing investigation to establish their alleged involvement in terrorist activities and identify possible links to other members of the network. It added that troops of 192 Battalion (Main), supported by Hybrid Force personnel at Hambagda Internally Displaced Persons (IDP) Camp in Gwoza, received a JAS member who surrendered at about 9:20 p.m. on Saturday. According to the report, preliminary investigation indicated that the individual had escaped from a terrorist enclave in the Mandara Mountains area of Gwoza and decided to abandon terrorism. “The individual surrendered with an AK-47 rifle and a magazine containing 28 rounds of 7.62mm special ammunition,” it added. The report said the defector was in custody undergoing further investigation and processing in line with established procedures. It said the operations underscore OPHK’s continued efforts to disrupt terrorist activities, dismantle support networks and encourage defections through sustained, intelligence-led operations. The military urged members of the public to provide credible and timely information to security agencies to support efforts to restore peace and enable displaced communities to return safely. Voters arrive at their polling units On election day, registered voters go to the polling units where their names appear on the voters’ register. They are expected to check their polling unit before leaving home to avoid going to the wrong location. At the polling unit, officials organise voters and direct them to the appropriate queues. Security personnel may also be present to maintain order and prevent disruptions. item.title: NDC to unveil campaign council, present financial statement at NEC meeting
item.description: The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) says it will unveil its National Campaign Council and present its statement of account at its third National Executive Committee (NEC) meeting scheduled for Monday, October 26, in Abuja. The party said the presentation of its financial statement was part of its commitment to transparency and accountability, challenging other political parties, particularly the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), to disclose details of their finances. The announcement was contained in a statement signed by the NDC National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, Esq. According to the statement, the meeting will hold at JD Event Centre, Kashim Ibrahim Way, opposite A-Class Park, Maitama, Abuja, at 10am. “A major highlight of the meeting will be the release and presentation of the party’s Statement of Account by the National Treasurer. This is in deference to our avowed commitment to the principles of transparency and accountability,” the statement said. The party challenged the APC and other political parties to follow its example in the management and disclosure of their finances. “In this regard, we challenge other political parties, especially the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), to emulate this level of openness and transparency in the management of their finances,” it added. The NDC also addressed speculation about its finances, saying its resources would have been more substantial but for the inability of many of its candidates to pay for nomination forms. The party attributed the situation to the economic hardship in the country, claiming that about 80 per cent of its candidates could not afford the expression of interest forms. “However, contrary to speculations in the public domain, and due to the level of poverty, hunger and deprivation in the country occasioned by the rudderless APC and its amorphous economic policies, about 80% of our candidates could not afford the Expression of Interest forms,” the statement said. It added that the party issued the forms free of charge to the affected candidates. The NDC further disclosed that the meeting would feature the unveiling of its National Campaign Council (NCC), which it said would cover campaigns for the presidential, National Assembly, governorship and state Houses of Assembly elections. The party also said its candidates would receive certificates of return for their respective offices. Describing itself as prepared for the 2027 general election, the NDC said it was determined to offer Nigerians what it called altruistic leadership. “The NDC is turbo-charged and ready to give Nigerians the altruistic leadership the nation deserves,” the statement said. item.title: Troops raid bandits enclave, rescue three kidnap victims in Kebbi
item.description: By Haruna Aliyu,Birnin Kebbi Troops of Sector 2, Operation Fansan Yamma, have rescued three kidnapped victims during an operation in Sakaba Local Government Area of Kebbi State. The victims were identified as Aisha Aminu, 46; Sumayya Aminu, 27; and Nana Abbas, 15. The rescue operation took place on Saturday, October 24, 2026, with two of the victims rescued at Makuku Village and the third at Dankolo Village. The development was disclosed in a statement made available to our correspondent on Sunday by the spokesman for the 8 Division, Nigerian Army, Lt. Col. Olaniyi Osoba. According to the statement, the operation was successfully concluded without any incident. “The victims were subsequently handed over to the District Head of Dirindaji, Alhaji Usman Muhammad, through the Chairman of Sakaba Local Government Area,” the statement said. The military described the operation as successful, noting that the rescued victims were transferred to the relevant local authorities after their recovery. “The operation was concluded successfully without any incident,” the statement added. Osoba reaffirmed the troops’ commitment to protecting residents and communities in the state, stressing that troops remained focused on their responsibility to safeguard lives and property. “Troops remain committed to the protection of lives and property,” the statement said. The rescue comes amid persistent security concerns in parts of Nigeria’s North-West, where kidnapping and other criminal activities have continued to threaten residents and disrupt community life. item.title: 2027: Sowore slams NDC, accuses Obi of renting party every election
item.description: The presidential candidate of the African Action Congress (AAC), Omoyele Sowore, has criticised the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) and accused its presidential candidate Peter Obi of renting political parties during election seasons. Sowore alleged that Obi’s political moves were not aimed at liberating Nigerians but at helping the ruling establishment deflect public anger and avoid accountability ahead of the 2027 general election. In a statement posted on X, Sowore accused the NDC of exploiting the political process, claiming that its leaders made ₦9 billion from the sale of nomination forms while running the party from their homes. “The same opportunists and packaged political frauds who made ₦9 billion from selling nomination forms while running a political party from their living rooms,” Sowore wrote, referring to the NDC. He described Obi as an unprincipled politician who, according to him, changes political platforms ahead of elections without offering a genuine challenge to the political establishment. “This is the problem with unprincipled politicians like Peter Obi, who rent political parties every election season, not to liberate Nigerians, but to…. divert public anger and evade the revolutionary consequences of their actions,” he said. Sowore also accused supporters of Obi and other political figures of attempting to discredit critics and distract Nigerians from what he described as the country’s underlying social and political problems. He named Osun State Governor Ademola Adeleke and Abia State Governor Alex Otti among those he alleged had helped promote narratives that distract from these issues. “But we cannot be fooled,” Sowore said, insisting that the politicians he criticised were delaying what he described as the liberation of Nigerians. The AAC candidate further alleged that Obi and his allies were not genuinely opposed to Tinubu’s administration but were instead seeking to manage opposition to the president without mounting a strong challenge to his government. “They don’t oppose Tinubu; they simply don’t want anyone to oppose him strongly enough to bring his disastrous reign to an end. Their politics is about managing opposition, not confronting the system,” he said. Sowore also referred to a remark attributed to Datti Baba-Ahmed, Obi’s former running mate in the 2023 presidential election, describing Tinubu as their “favourite uncle”. Obi, who contested the 2023 presidential election on the platform of the Labour Party, has since moved to the NDC ahead of the 2027 election. item.title: Obama blasts Trump’s ‘chaos and cruelty’ while campaigning for Democrats
item.description: Former US president Barack Obama delivered scathing criticisms of his successor, Donald Trump, at rallies Saturday in Ohio and Michigan to support Democratic candidates ahead of the November 3 midterm elections. Democrats are attempting to wrest back control of one or both chambers of the US Congress, which are currently controlled by Trump’s Republican party. The former president retains considerable popularity among the Democratic base, which he is keen to leverage to support his Democratic Party’s candidates. In both states, the 65-year-old former president blamed the Trump administration for the rising cost of living, a top voter concern amid soaring fuel prices. “The current president chose to make a series of bad decisions,” Obama said in Ohio, where he rallied in support of former Democratic senator Sherrod Brown. “Most importantly, he decided to start an unnecessary war that nobody asked for.” “After two years of chaos and cruelty and corruption and incompetence, the likes of which we have not seen in the modern era, you get a chance to say, ‘Enough is enough,'” Obama declared in Cleveland. “We are voting for change right here in Ohio.” Later, in Michigan, Obama campaigned for Abdul El-Sayed, from the party’s left wing, who is in a close race with Republican Mike Rogers for the US Senate. “Imagine the power duo of Abdul and Elissa,” Obama said, referring to the incumbent Democratic Senator Elissa Slotkin, who is not up for election this year. “You got a Muslim man, you got a Jewish woman fighting for you in the United States Senate. That’s something, Michigan, you can be proud of.” Obama also urged voters to cast their ballots as soon as possible since early voting is already open in both states. “Don’t procrastinate, don’t equivocate,” Obama said. In Ohio, Brown will attempt a comeback against incumbent Republican Senator Jon Husted, while the race for governor will be contested between Democrat Amy Acton and Republican Vivek Ramaswamy, a former presidential candidate in 2024. Polls for Ohio give Democrats a slight lead in both those races, but the results are expected to be close. Obama also took digs at Trump’s renovation projects across the US capital, including his botched renovation of the National Mall’s Reflecting Pool, his construction of a massive White House Ballroom and the guilded decorations he has adorned the Oval Office with during his second tenure. “He’s got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory,” Obama said, referring to popular but indulgent American restaurant chain. Ecological interventions The erosion and flood-control component of the programme covers a range of communities where the government has listed projects intended to address erosion, flooding and deteriorating road infrastructure. The project schedule contains 32 entries, including the construction of bridges and culverts for flood control, erosion-control works, remediation of affected areas and road improvement along selected routes. Among the locations listed are Zambur, Unguwar Gai in Kibiya Local Government Area, Rimmin Yamma and Sumaila, Rurum-Bunkini-Kazaurawa, Furuwa, Kibiya town bypass, Zango and Hanyar Kogo in Takai, Kachako, Karaye, Kukar Bashari and Kwanar Dan Goro. Other locations include Fulatan in Rogo Local Government Area, Kadabo Road, Darki bypass in Wudil, Kiru, Tiga-Runum Road, Gala, Wudil town, Daki community, Bebejii, Kadauji village and Magami. The programme also lists road improvement and erosion-control works along Sabon Gwandu, Kazaurewa-Gana Road in Rano, Unguwar Gora, Rano-Bunkure Road and Falali in Sumaila, among other locations. The projects vary in their stated purposes. Some are primarily concerned with erosion control, while others combine erosion remediation with road improvement. Several involve the construction of bridges or culverts intended to help manage flooding and improve movement within affected communities. Such infrastructure can be important in rural areas where roads provide links between farms, residential settlements, markets and other essential services. Where erosion damages roads or floodwaters cut off access, farmers may encounter additional difficulties moving produce to buyers, obtaining agricultural inputs or reaching their fields. The listed interventions therefore have potential implications beyond the physical structures being constructed. Their value to communities will depend on whether they address the problems for which they were designed and whether the infrastructure remains functional after construction. Challenge of flooding, erosion Flooding and erosion can place considerable pressure on communities whose livelihoods depend on agriculture and local trade. Heavy rainfall can wash away topsoil, damage roads, undermine structures and disrupt the movement of people and goods. Where water is poorly channelled, runoff can gradually erode the land, deepen gullies and threaten farmland and residential areas. Flooding can also make roads impassable, leaving some communities with limited access to markets and essential services. For farming households, the effects may extend beyond the immediate damage. The loss of productive land, interruption of cultivation and difficulty transporting harvested crops can affect household earnings and food availability. The Federal Government’s programme addresses some of these concerns through a combination of erosion-control structures, bridges, culverts and road improvement works. The inclusion of bridges and culverts in locations such as Zambur, Furuwa, Magami and Unguwar Gora suggests an effort to address specific points where water movement and access are important considerations. Other projects focus on erosion remediation or the improvement of roads in towns and rural settlements. However, without adequate maintenance, infrastructure intended to control erosion and flooding can deteriorate, reducing its effectiveness over time. The programme’s long-term value will therefore depend not only on construction but also on the quality of the works, their suitability for local conditions and the arrangements for monitoring and maintenance. Irrigation expansion While the erosion and flood-control projects address environmental and infrastructure challenges, the irrigation component seeks to improve access to water for agriculture. The EPO has listed interventions at Tiga, Challawa-Gorge and Kafin Chiri dams, with plans to open new sectors for irrigation and provide canal networks to serve designated areas of farmland. Together, the three schemes are designed to cover 1,279.91 hectares. The Tiga Dam intervention accounts for 875 hectares, Challawa-Gorge for 240 hectares and Kafin Chiri for 164.91 hectares. The proposed schemes combine main canals, distribution canals, field canals and pipe extensions, depending on the requirements of each location. The objective, according to the documents, was to make water available for cultivation beyond the main rainy season, giving farmers an opportunity to grow crops during periods when rainfall alone may not support production. Dry-season farming can provide an additional source of income for farmers and help maintain agricultural activity when rain-fed cultivation is no longer possible. Depending on local conditions, crops grown under irrigation can also supply markets at different times of the year. For the intervention to achieve these aims, however, the infrastructure must be completed, supplied with adequate water and operated in a way that allows farmers to use it reliably. Tiga Dam: 875 hectares earmarked for irrigation The Tiga Dam scheme is the largest of the three irrigation interventions listed in the project material. Completed in 1974, Tiga Dam is a major water-storage structure associated with the Kano River Irrigation Project. The supplied technical data describes it as a zoned earth-fill dam with a length of 6,000 metres and a maximum height of 48 metres from foundation level.

The road to Aso Rock in 2027 runs through two regions where elections can be won, lost or thrown wide open: the North-West and South-West. Their combined electoral strength gives them enormous influence over the calculations of President Bola Tinubu and the opposition figures seeking to unseat him. The Independent National Electoral Commission’s 2026 voter register puts the North-West at 25,083,411 registered voters and the South-West at 19,614,274. Together, they account for 44,697,685 registered voters, representing more than 43 per cent of Nigeria’s 103,428,715 registered voters ahead of the 2027 general elections. Those figures make the two zones central to the presidential contest. But the real battle is more complicated than regional arithmetic. Candidates must convert registered voters into ballots, hold their traditional strongholds, penetrate rival territories and build a coalition broad enough to survive the country’s political and geographical divisions. What elections since 1999 reveal Nigeria’s presidential elections have repeatedly shown that regional strength matters most when it forms part of a wider national coalition. Olusegun Obasanjo’s victories in 1999 and 2003 rested on support extending beyond his South-West origins. Umaru Musa Yar’Adua’s 2007 victory reflected the strength of the Peoples Democratic Party’s national machinery, while Goodluck Jonathan’s 2011 success drew on substantial support in the South and parts of the North. The 2015 election changed the political landscape. Muhammadu Buhari’s victory demonstrated that an opposition alliance could defeat an incumbent when it combined a formidable northern base with support in other parts of the country. The merger that produced the All Progressives Congress brought together political interests that had previously competed against one another. Buhari’s re-election in 2019 again showed the importance of maintaining a broad electoral coalition, even as the contest exposed persistent regional divisions. For infectious disease experts, Nigeria’s latest Ebola alert is a reminder that preparedness cannot be measured by emergency announcements alone. It must be evident in the wards, consultation rooms and emergency units where patients first seek care. One confirmed case, a nationwide test Nigeria’s latest Ebola alert followed the confirmation of an imported case of Bundibugyo virus disease in the Federal Capital Territory on October 20, 2026. According to the World Health Organisation (WHO), the patient, a woman with a recent travel history involving Uganda, developed symptoms on October 7 and sought treatment at a private hospital in Abuja on October 11. Laboratory tests confirmed the infection on October 20. Authorities identified 44 contacts for monitoring, including people who might have been exposed during the patient’s healthcare visits and travel. The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) activated its incident management system, while surveillance and infection-prevention measures were strengthened. By October 23, the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Muhammad Ali Pate, said the patient was showing signs of recovery. There was no evidence of community transmission in the information released at that point, although investigations and contact monitoring were continuing. Genomic analysis also found that the virus detected in Nigeria was genetically related to the strain identified in Kenya’s index case. Pate cautioned that this similarity did not, by itself, establish a direct epidemiological link between the two patients or explain precisely how the infection reached Nigeria. The response is therefore unfolding on two fronts. Authorities must establish whether anyone else has been infected, while ensuring that hospitals can recognise and safely manage any suspected cases that emerge. Second responsibility That second responsibility is particularly important. A patient with fever, headache, vomiting or diarrhoea may have any of several illnesses. But when the symptoms are accompanied by a relevant exposure history, health workers must know what questions to ask, whom to notify and how to protect themselves and others while the patient is assessed. An outbreak may be detected by a laboratory, but preventing further transmission also depends on what happens at the patient’s first point of contact with the health system. When the basics cannot be taken for granted Running water, soap, hand sanitisers, cleaning materials, protective equipment and safe waste disposal rarely command the attention given to emergency operations centres or laboratory testing. Yet these ordinary provisions underpin the safe delivery of healthcare. A tap without water cannot support handwashing. An empty sanitiser dispenser offers little protection. Personal protective equipment that is missing when needed can leave a health worker unable to follow the precautions required when caring for a suspected infectious case. The problem is not necessarily that every Nigerian hospital lacks these facilities. It is that their availability, functionality and reliability cannot be assumed. A UNICEF Nigeria WASH Gender Landscape Analysis published in January 2025 reported that only six per cent of healthcare facilities assessed had basic water, sanitation and hygiene services. The figure relates to the facilities covered by the assessment, rather than every hospital in the country, but it highlights a significant infrastructure challenge. For Ebola preparedness, the implications are immediate. Infection prevention is not simply a matter of displaying instructions on a hospital wall. It requires dependable water supplies, adequate consumables, appropriate protective equipment, trained staff and systems that ensure these resources are available where and when they are needed. item.title: VIDEO: ‘Tinubu Fought For You’, Shettima Seeks North’s Support For Tinubu’s Re-Election
item.description: Vice President Kashim Shettima has appealed to voters in northern Nigeria to back President Bola Tinubu for a second term in 2027, arguing that the President has earned the region’s support through his past backing of northern political leaders. Shettima made the appeal on Saturday at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign flag-off in Kaduna, where he urged voters to support the party’s candidates across all levels of government. “We have come to ask you to renew a second time for the APC from top to bottom,” he said. The Vice President cited Tinubu’s support for northern figures, including former President Muhammadu Buhari, as a reason for voters in the region to reciprocate by supporting his re-election bid.
